analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md. Per the patch, two hunks touch it. One edits the fixtures paragraph near head lines 958-960, which now reads "`coordinator/tests/protocol/testdata/process_memory_wire.json` are fixtures". The other replaces the "Retained Console" test section (head ~1084-1088) with a short "Console" section saying console tests run in the platform repository. No source, crypto, authorization, attestation, cache or build-script behavior changes.

I read both supplied head-text units (lines 1-939 of the document). They are unchanged documentation covering provider tests, SSD/KV checkpoint qualification, App Attest resumption and logout, add-on hold, watchdog, native serving qualification and fixtures. The tests and env flags they describe carry the existing guidance on isolated state, no production cache roots or keys, and no live provider credentials. Nothing there widens attack surface or contradicts threat entries T-041, T-053, T-059, T-060 or TB-011/TB-012.

Two minor observations, neither a security regression. First, the edited fixtures sentence now reads awkwardly: the patch drops the sentence start and the paged_footprint_wire.json mention may be partially lost. That is a documentation-quality issue only. Second, removal of the retained console lane documentation reflects an ownership move to the platform repo. Whether this repo's CI or hooks were actually removed is outside the supplied evidence, so I treat it as an unverified contract rather than a finding. Console tests exercise out-of-scope surface per the canonical scope.

No evidence suggests disabled security tests. Remaining integration question: confirm the Makefile and CI do not still reference the removed ui-* targets. That is a build-consistency matter, not a security one.
